title: Hector: An Efficient Programming and Compilation Framework for Implementing Relational Graph Neural Networks in GPU Architectures
problem: RGNNs exhibit memory-intensive computation patterns and a significant gap between high-level programming interfaces and GPU kernel APIs, requiring extensive manual optimization effort tightly coupled to data layout and heterogeneity.
motivation: RGNNs are increasingly adopted in real-world applications for versatility and accuracy, but deployment faces performance challenges and high programming complexity.
method: Hector proposes a two-level intermediate representation (IR) and code generator that captures RGNN properties and inter-operator scheduling opportunities, generates flexible data access schemes to eliminate redundant copies, and decouples model semantics, data layout, and operator-specific optimizations. The framework builds on general GEMM and node/edge traversal templates with linear operator reordering and compact materialization techniques.
key_novelty: A two-level IR framework that decouples model semantics, data layout, and operator-specific optimizations to enable efficient RGNN compilation while reducing programming effort from thousands of lines to 51 lines of input.
contributions: Two-level IR capturing RGNN properties and inter-operator scheduling opportunities for memory efficiency
Code generation with flexible data access schemes eliminating redundant copies
Decoupling of model semantics, data layout, and optimizations reducing programming complexity
Linear operator reordering and compact materialization techniques providing up to 3.8× additional acceleration

metrics.speedup: 9.9× inference, 43.7× training on RGCN, RGAT, HGT models
metrics.other: No OOM exceptions; 3.8× additional speedup from operator reordering and materialization

limitations: Paper does not discuss generalization beyond the three tested RGNN models or scalability to extremely large graphs.
primary_theme: GPU compilation framework for relational graph neural networks
